Hi Erin — great questions, and thanks for the sample usage. Short answer up front: we try to avoid double-charging customers for the same active user context, but behavior depends on whether KV/prefix is warm and the configured aggregation window. Full details below so procurement has a single doc to reference.

Overview (high level):
- Minimum quantum applies per "billing unit" which is normally a request when no session aggregation applies.
- We have a configurable session aggregation window (default 60s) that groups requests with the same conversation id into one billing bucket for minimums.
- KV warming matters: pulling a cold 6k context incurs extra compute but we apply a short amortization credit when subsequent requests reuse the same prefix within the aggregation window.

Key implications for BrightCart:
1) If your three short calls happen within the same conversation id and within the aggregation window, they'll be bucketized together for the minimum; token counts still accumulate for charge-by-token.
2) Cold KV fetchs are billed as compute; however, if KV hits are frequent we give a partial amortization (see attached proration matrix).
3) For SOW clarity we can set the aggregation window and define a higher-tier default for dedicated pools to reduce cold-fetch impact.

I'll let Kim add the exact math and sample invoice lines. Sergio — want me to propose wording for the SOW amendment about aggregation/window and amortization credits?

Hi Erin, Vanessa — following up with concrete examples and the invoicing logic. I ran the BrightCart sample through our proration calculator; output attached. High-level rules we used: 

Billing primitives: 
- Token charge: per-token generated/consumed (no rounding).
- Minimum quantum: applied per billing bucket; default quantum = 256 tokens.
- Aggregation window: default = 60s (configurable at account level).
- KV cold fetch surcharge: one-time compute surcharge charged on first fetch per prefix, then amortized across subsequent requests within the warm period.

Example (from your CSV):
- User A: 3 calls in 90s with same convo id. Sequence: call1 (200 tokens, cold fetch 6k), call2 (180 tokens, warm), call3 (220 tokens, warm).
  - Token lines: 200+180+220 = 600 tokens billed at token rate.
  - Minimums: since call1 and call2 are within 60s, call1+call2 bucketize (min quantum applies once); call3 falls outside 60s -> separate min quantum.
  - Result: one minimum applied for bucket1 (ceil(380/256) = 2 quanta if you measure minima by quantum count) and one for bucket2.

Proration/Amortization:
- KV cold fetch surcharge will appear as a distinct invoice line but we apply a 40% amortization credit across warm hits within the warm window for BrightCart pilot pricing.

SOW language suggestion (short):
"Redwood will apply session aggregation for minimum-calculation with a default window of 60 seconds. Cold KV fetches are billed as a one-time compute surcharge per prefix; Redwood will amortize up to 40% of that surcharge across subsequent warm hits within the warm period for pilot customers. The aggregation window and amortization percent are negotiable per SOW."

I've attached the proration matrix PDF and a CSV with per-user simulated invoice lines. Let me know if you want a worked invoice sample with your actual rates plugged in.
